sentences.text: Palaeocarcharias resembled carpet sharks and reached a total body length of about 1 meter.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Palaeocarcharias as Lamniformes.
A 2018 study proposed classifying it as the sole member of the order Palaeocarchariiformes, while a 2023 study favored placing it within Lamniformes.
The genus lived from the Bathonian to the Tithonian, between 168.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
Isolated teeth from England suggest the genus Palaeocarcharias existed back to the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian).
A 2024 study suggested that a specimen from Canjuers might actually be a true carpet shark belonging to Orectolobidae.
